title: Haluski (Buttery Cabbage and Egg Noodles)
summary: Wide egg noodles tossed with cabbage and onion cooked slowly until soft, sweet and browned in patches, finished with butter and plenty of black pepper.
equipment: large casserole or very large deep frying pan with lid (at least 30 cm)

ingredients.item: green or white cabbage, cored and thinly sliced
fine sea salt or table salt
fine salt for 3 litres of pasta water (0.8%)
ingredients.note: about 4 tsp; most of it goes down the drain
optional, to serve on the side

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Melt the 60 g of butter in a large casserole or deep frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the onion for 4-5 minutes, until soft and lightly browned.

steps.title: Steam the cabbage
steps.text: Add the cabbage, salt and pepper and toss to coat, then cover and lower the heat to medium-low. Cook for 30 minutes, stirring every 5-10 minutes, until the cabbage turns silky and tender - it will shrink down to about a third of its original volume, as the cover traps steam that softens it gently.

steps.title: Brown the cabbage
steps.text: Uncover the pan, raise the heat to medium, and cook for a further 10-15 minutes, stirring often, until the cabbage turns golden and sweet in patches. Add a tablespoon of water if it starts to catch on the bottom - this browning is what turns the cabbage's sharper, sulphury notes into something nutty and sweet.

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.text: Bring 3 litres of water to the boil with the 24 g salt and cook the egg noodles to the packet time. Reserve 240 ml of the cooking water, then drain.

steps.title: Combine and toss
steps.text: Add the noodles, 120 ml of the reserved water and the 15 g of butter to the cabbage, and stir over medium-high heat for 1-2 minutes until everything looks glossy. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with an extra grind of black pepper, the chopped dill if using, and the sour cream on the side for anyone who wants it.

tips: Don't rush the covered cooking stage - cabbage needs the full 30 minutes to collapse down and turn tender rather than staying crunchy.
Let the cabbage brown properly once uncovered; stopping too early leaves it merely soft, missing the sweeter, nuttier flavour that comes from browning.
Keep a splash of water nearby during the browning stage in case the cabbage starts to catch and burn on the bottom of the pan.
Reserve some pasta water before draining the noodles, since it's easy to forget and the dish relies on it to bring everything together.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a pan with a splash of water over medium heat, stirring, until piping hot throughout. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
